recommended_merges.recommended_statement: Under the canonical principal-part identification gr_n≅Lie(E)^n, invariant differentiation has graded symbol -n times multiplication by the tangent vector. The symbol is invertible where n is a unit and is zero in characteristic p when p divides n. A multiplicative renormalization epsilon_n=c^n pp_n changes it to -nc, never to1 in every degree. Cote62 gives the correct unit/vanishing qualification; the unrestricted coefficient-one arrows in cote64 are false under any multiplicative convention.

Cote62's normalization announcement, its barycentric continuation, and late64's explicit complement illuminate this distinction, but are not identical assertions with identical hypotheses.

links_not_merges.rationale: Defining invariant differentiation, identifying principal parts, computing its graded symbol, determining its full p-kernel, distinguishing the Rees ring from the filtered union, and normalizing the cubic coefficient are different assertions. Their connection is essential, especially because a graded-symbol failure alone does not calculate the full kernel.

All involve central sign extensions, but their quotient groups and moduli problems differ: an affine-coordinate group, the D8 two-character extension controlling projective mod-four lifts, and the later order12 pinning group over S3. No isomorphism of these extensions is asserted by the common word central.
